facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
no breast symptoms
routine screening mammography
a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast
no discrete abnormality corresponding to the mammographic finding
tomosynthesis-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy of the right inner breast
12 core specimens
marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils, with lymphocytes and plasma cells and no granulomata
no history of urticaria, asthma, angioedema, or pruritus except for seasonal allergic rhinitis
Peripheral blood eosinophil levels were within the normal range
Hypereosinophilic syndrome was excluded from consideration
asymptomatic

concepts.why: The patient has a developing asymmetry in the right breast with chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, which is consistent with chronic inflammatory breast disease.
The patient has a marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils, which is consistent with eosinophilic mastitis.

The patient has a developing asymmetry in the right breast with chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, which could be consistent with idiopathic granulomatous mastitis, although no granulomata were seen.
The patient has a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis, which is consistent with allergic rhinitis.
The patient has a chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, which could be consistent with sclerosing lymphocytic lobulitis.
The patient has a chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, which could be consistent with lymphocytic lobulitis.
The patient has a chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, which could be consistent with periductal mastitis.
The patient has a marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils, which could be consistent with eosinophilic allergic panniculitis.

rationales.F04: Developing asymmetry in the breast is a common finding in various breast diseases.
rationales.F08: The presence of a mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils is a key feature of certain breast diseases.
rationales.F11: The exclusion of hypereosinophilic syndrome is important in the differential diagnosis of breast diseases with eosinophilic infiltrates.
